problem.name: Optimal polynomial intersection
problem.statement_latex:
Given prime $p$, integer $n<p-1$, and explicit sets $F_y\subseteq\mathbb F_p$ for $y\ne0$, find a polynomial $Q\in\mathbb F_p[y]$, $\deg Q<n$, maximizing $|\{y:Q(y)\in F_y\}|$. The approximation task asks for a specified fraction of the $p-1$ constraints. This connects finite-field fitting, list recovery and coding theory.
The explicit-input comparison counts quantum gates and classical finite-field operations; the folded-OPI separation counts membership-oracle queries.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(p)$ gates, decoded quantum interferometry for the stated balanced OPI regime.
quantum.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(p)$ gates, decoded quantum interferometry for the stated balanced OPI regime.
quantum.details_latex: With $|F_y|\approx p/2$ and constant $n/p$, DQI achieves fraction $1/2+\sqrt{(n/(2p))(1-n/(2p))}$ asymptotically, using efficient decoding of the relevant Reed--Solomon dual code. Horinaga--Yamakawa give a worst-case polynomial-time quantum algorithm with full satisfaction for balanced sets at rate above $3/4$. For the folded membership-oracle family at rate $0.3$, the separation gives expected quantum score $0.85$ while a classical score exceeding $0.65$ by a constant requires superpolynomially many queries.

classical.headline_latex: Polynomial-time interpolation with expected fraction $1/2+n/(2p)$, Prange-type interpolation; exponential repetition to reach the studied DQI target.
classical.headline_text: Polynomial-time interpolation with expected fraction $1/2+n/(2p)$, Prange-type interpolation; exponential repetition to reach the studied DQI target.
classical.details_latex: Complete enumeration costs $p^n\operatorname{poly}(p,n)$. The explicit balanced tables contain $\Theta(p^2)$ bits. A direct Boolean objective circuit has $O(pn\log^2p+p^2\log p)$ gates, so applying subexponential exact counting to this circuit gives a bound whose exponent, at constant $n/p$, exceeds the studied exponential-in-$p$ interpolation-repetition comparator. The oracle lower bound concerns unknown acceptance tables in the folded family.

strength.description_latex: Candidate exponential-to-polynomial advantage for the explicit random-instance approximation target; a superpolynomial query separation for the folded oracle family. The mechanism is decoded Fourier interference.

evidence.description_latex: Partial evidence for the explicit-input comparison, based on the analyzed classical algorithms. The folded oracle comparison has a rigorous classical query lower bound.

hardware.description_latex: Fault-tolerant DQI requires approximately $O((p+n)\log p)$ logical data qubits plus decoding workspace. A cited $p=521$ design uses about 8,850 logical qubits and $1.01\times10^8$ Toffoli gates; decoder construction and error correction determine physical scale.
